mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N more grapes than Y', translate it to the signed equation X = Y + N (or X - Y = N). Without this, the model may reverse the sign and set X = Y - N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the phrase 'has N more' (or 'more than') relating two individuals.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has 5 more grapes than Y' as X = Y - 5.

mathgap.title: Signed relational equation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, such as 'the number of grapes that X has more than Y equals the difference between A and B', write a linear equation X - Y = A - B. Without this, the model may treat the differences as separate absolute values rather than an equality of signed differences.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement compares two differences.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'the number of grapes that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between A and B' as X = Y + (A - B) instead of X - Y = A - B.

mathgap.title: Allow negative differences
mathgap.principle: Do not assume that a 'more than' or 'difference' clause yields a positive result; keep the sign as indicated, allowing for negative differences (e.g., 'has N fewer' translates to X = Y - N). Without this, the model may force a positive offset and get the sign wrong.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses 'fewer' or when the computed difference could be negative.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has 3 fewer grapes than Y' as X = Y + 3.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: Each transfer 'X gives N to Y' reduces X by N and increases Y by N; apply these net changes to the current counts. Without this, the model may add N to both parties or forget to subtract from the giver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly describes a transfer of a known quantity.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X gives 5 grapes to Y' as X = X + 5, Y = Y + 5.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Represent each person as a variable and write a linear equation for every relational, transfer, split, redistribution, increase, or absolute count statement, treating absolute counts as constraints on final values and ensuring each name is a distinct variable. Solve the resulting system simultaneously. Without this, the model may miss constraints or conflate variables.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After parsing all statements, before attempting to compute the answer.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Ismael has 2 grapes' as an initial count before transfers, leading to double‑counting.

mathgap.title: Combined sum interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'X has N more grapes than Y and Z combined', translate to X = (Y + Z) + N (or X - (Y + Z) = N). Without this, the model may omit the combined sum or misplace the offset.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement references a sum of multiple people.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has 5 more grapes than Y and Z combined' as X = Y + 5 or X = Z + 5.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by k times', multiply the current count by k (new = old * k). For fractional factors, multiply accordingly. Without this, the model may add instead of multiply.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses 'increases by' followed by a multiplier.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X increases by 2 times' as X = X + 2.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'splits all the grapes she owns equally among A and B', set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient half of the splitter's original amount. When a statement says 'redistribute ... to ensure each has an equal amount', pool their grapes and give each half of the total. Without this, the model may leave the splitter with some grapes or mis‑allocate the total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a split or redistribution statement appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X splits all grapes equally among A and B' as X keeps half of the grapes.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form 'If X has more than N grapes, X will transfer their grapes to Y', first evaluate X's current count; if it exceeds N, set X to 0 and add its previous count to Y; otherwise, do nothing. Without this, the model may always transfer or ignore the condition.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a conditional transfer clause appears.
mathgap.example: Applying the transfer even when X has 0 grapes, because the condition 'more than 1' is false.

mathgap.title: Switch operation handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X and Y switch the grapes they have', exchange the entire counts of X and Y (X becomes Y's previous count and vice versa). Without this, the model may treat it as a one‑way transfer or ignore the swap.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X and Y switch the grapes they have' as X giving all grapes to Y while Y keeps theirs.

mathgap.description: Treating 'X has N' as an initial count before transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that 'X has N' describes the starting quantity, leading to double‑counting when later transfers are applied.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret absolute count statements as constraints on the final values; incorporate them into the system of equations rather than as pre‑transfer amounts.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a split as a simple division without zeroing the splitter, or misapplies the equal‑share rule for redistribution.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When splitting, set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient half of the original amount; when redistributing, pool the grapes and assign each participant half of the total.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the source and destination of a transfer.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement says 'X gives N to Y', decrease X by N and increase Y by N.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats the conditional clause as irrelevant or mis‑evaluates the inequality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: First evaluate the condition (e.g., X > N); only apply the transfer if the condition is satisfied.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model does not recognize that 'switch' means exchanging the entire counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement says 'X and Y switch the grapes they have', swap the values of X and Y.
